format: Native1920×1080 full-canvas H.264CRF17,30fps,AAC160k. No source-image scaling, side borders, custom framing panels or title strips.
voice: en-US-JennyNeural, public generic narration only; actual consenting call audio reused unchanged except loudness/short fades.
environments: Approved real-call saved snapshot verified in production and copied unchanged into isolated current app for clean display; fictional workflow actions in same app. No production case changes.

scenes.name: 01-welcome
scenes.text: When someone needs help, a phone call should be enough. Pharos turns that call into a clear next step for responders.

scenes.name: 02-real-call
scenes.text: Here’s a short excerpt from a real call.

scenes.name: 03-transcript
scenes.text: That call is now complete. The team can read the generated transcript, check consent, and open the linked request. Nothing has to be copied by hand.

scenes.name: 04-overview
scenes.text: Overview brings the essentials together: where the caller is, what they need, and why the request is ranked this way. These are reported facts for people to review.

scenes.name: 05-review
scenes.text: For this fictional training report, the team needs to check a concern. The quoted words stay beside the request. Reported danger keeps its urgency while normal response actions wait for human review.

scenes.name: 06-assignment
scenes.text: The reviewer records a reason and accepts the report. Now an eligible responder can take ownership. That decision stays tied to the evidence, so everyone can see what was checked.

scenes.name: 07-progress
scenes.text: Here, the desk reports that the responder is on the way and gives a ten-minute estimate. A claim alone never promises travel, and an estimate is not a guarantee.

scenes.name: 08-history
scenes.text: History keeps the report and human decisions together. When new information arrives, the team can look back, reassess the situation, and update the next step.

scenes.name: 09-coverage
scenes.text: Coverage shows which approved teams serve each area, what help they can offer, and whether they have room for another request.

scenes.name: 10-training
scenes.text: The training lab lets teams practice with a prepared fictional report. Process it once, then review the new case. That’s Pharos: a clearer handoff from a caller to the people who can help.
